features.name: Safari content blocker with bundled rules
features.description: One or more Safari Content Blocker extensions load JSON rules that block ad, tracker and crypto-mining requests and hide ad elements with CSS selectors. Rules ship inside the app bundle and are split across several extensions to stay under Safari's per-extension rule limit.
features.reason: This is the whole product. It runs entirely on-device through Safari's declarative content blocking API, with no network access needed.

features.name: Blocking category toggles
features.description: Separate on/off switches for Ads, Trackers, Cookie & consent banners, Annoyances (newsletter, notification-permission and 'open in app' prompts, sign-in nags, anti-adblock walls, floating video players) and Crypto mining. Changing a switch rebuilds the rule files in the App Group container and calls SFContentBlockerManager.reloadContentBlocker.
features.reason: Reviewers asked to configure what gets blocked. The most common case is turning off cookie-banner hiding, because hidden consent banners leave some sites unusable.

features.name: Allowed sites list
features.description: The user can add domains where blocking is turned off. These are compiled into an ignore-previous-rules entry with if-domain, and the list can be edited and swiped to delete.
features.reason: Gives users a quick way to fix a site that breaks under blocking, without turning everything off. Fully local.

features.name: Status and setup check
features.description: The home screen shows whether each extension is enabled in Safari Settings (via getStateOfContentBlocker), how many rules are active, and when they were last compiled. A Refresh button recompiles the bundled rules and reloads the extensions.
features.reason: Users can't tell if the blocker is working, and many 'it doesn't block anything' reviews likely come from extensions that aren't enabled. In the remake, refresh means recompiling locally, not downloading.

features.name: Guided setup
features.description: Step-by-step screens show how to enable each extension in Settings > Apps > Safari > Extensions. They point to Safari's built-in Block Pop-ups setting and suggest a restart of Safari after changes.
features.reason: Setup is the main source of perceived failure. Everything is static, on-device content.

features.name: Regional language lists
features.description: Optional bundled rule sets for non-English sites, chosen per language (e.g. Italian, German, French, Japanese). They are compiled into the rule files only when enabled.
features.reason: Improves blocking of regional ads. The lists are bundled and update with app releases, so no network is needed.

features.name: Custom element-hiding rules
features.description: Advanced users can add their own rules as domain plus CSS selector to hide extra elements. Each rule is checked for basic syntax before compiling.
features.reason: Lets users fix leftover ads themselves while waiting for app updates. Local only.

features.name: Scriptlet web extension for stubborn sites
features.description: An optional Safari Web Extension that injects bundled scripts on specific sites. Examples: neutralising click-triggered window.open popups and redirects, and skipping in-video ads. It also offers a toolbar button to allow the current site.
features.reason: Declarative rules cannot stop popups, new tabs or video ads, which are the top complaints. This needs website-access permission and ongoing maintenance, so it should ship as an opt-in with honest expectations.

features.name: Universal app and accessibility
features.description: The same app runs on iPhone, iPad and Mac (Catalyst or native) with full VoiceOver, Dynamic Type and Voice Control labels. Alternate dark and tinted icons are included.
features.reason: Matches the paid app's platform reach at no extra cost.

features.name: Automatic twice-weekly blocklist downloads
features.description: The paid app fetches updated filter lists from a server in the background.
features.reason: Requires network access and a server. In the remake, rules are refreshed through regular App Store updates instead.

features.name: System-wide network-level blocking add-on
features.description: A separate add-on that filters ad and tracker domains in all apps at the network level.
features.reason: Needs a network extension (DNS or tunnel) and network-level traffic handling, which is outside Sbu's no-network, one-thing scope.

features.name: Tip jar
features.description: In-app purchase tips for the developer.
features.reason: Sbu apps have no in-app purchases.

features.name: About developer / social links
features.description: A page linking to the developer's Mastodon, Bluesky, website and blog.
features.reason: Branding and external network links, which don't belong in a no-network remake.

screens.name: Home / Status
screens.purpose: Show at a glance whether blocking is active and up to date
elements: Calm full-screen background with a large status line (e.g. 'Blocking is active' / 'Enable in Settings')
Per-extension enabled indicators
Active rule count and last compiled date
Refresh button that recompiles and reloads the extensions
More button that opens the menu sheet

screens.name: Setup Guide
screens.purpose: Walk the user through enabling the Safari extensions
elements: Numbered steps with SF Symbols
Open Settings button
Live checkmarks as each extension becomes enabled
Tip about Safari's built-in Block Pop-ups setting

screens.name: Blocking Options
screens.purpose: Choose which kinds of things to block
elements: Toggle list: Ads, Trackers, Cookie & consent banners, Annoyances, Crypto mining
Explanatory footer per toggle (e.g. note that hiding cookie banners can break some sites)
Regional languages section with a multi-select list
Rebuilding progress indicator

screens.name: Allowed Sites
screens.purpose: Turn off blocking on specific domains
elements: List of domains with swipe-to-delete
Add field that normalises pasted URLs to a domain
Empty state explaining when to use this

screens.name: Custom Rules
elements: List of domain + CSS selector rules
Add/edit form with validation
Enable/disable switch per rule

screens.name: More / Help
screens.purpose: Menu sheet with help and app info
elements: Close button
Help / FAQ (why ads may still appear, YouTube limits, how to report)
Privacy statement: no data leaves the device
Version and rules bundle date

flows.name: First launch setup
steps: Open the app; status shows 'Not enabled'
Tap Set Up and follow the guide
Tap Open Settings and enable the extensions under Safari > Extensions
Return to the app; status re-checks on foreground and shows active with the rule count

flows.name: Fix a site broken by a hidden cookie banner
steps: Turn off Cookie & consent banners, or go to Allowed Sites
App rebuilds the rules and reloads the extensions
Reload the page in Safari; the banner appears and can be accepted

flows.name: Add a regional language list
steps: Select a language under Regional lists
Rules are merged and compiled into the App Group container
Extensions reload and the status rule count updates

flows.name: Manual refresh
steps: App recompiles all enabled sets from bundled sources plus user settings
Each content blocker is reloaded and any compile errors are surfaced

fields.name: cookieBannersEnabled
fields.note: default true; users often switch this off

fields.name: regionalLanguages
fields.note: language codes of bundled regional lists to include

fields.name: domain
fields.note: normalised host, compiled into an ignore-previous-rules entry

fields.name: bundledRulesVersion
fields.note: date of the shipped filter snapshot

data_model.storage: Settings, allowed sites and custom rules live in App Group UserDefaults or a small JSON/SwiftData store shared with the extensions. Compiled rule JSON files are written to the App Group container and read by each content blocker's NSExtensionRequestHandling. Source filter lists are bundled in the app. No network calls, no analytics.

monetization.notes: No in-app purchases, tips, ads, account or tracking. The paid app charges again for version 2, which reviewers resented; the remake should keep all features free and update its bundled rules through regular app releases.

user_pains.pain: Ads still show up / blocks little or nothing
user_pains.evidence: Reviews say there's no noticeable difference, it doesn't block anything, and not all ads are blocked.

user_pains.pain: Paid again for version 2 / too expensive compared with free blockers
user_pains.evidence: Reviewers resent re-buying after owning v1, find the price high, and say free extensions work as well.

user_pains.pain: Popups, new tabs and redirects not blocked
user_pains.evidence: Starting a video opens a popup that redirects elsewhere; pop-ups and tabs keep appearing.

user_pains.pain: YouTube ads not blocked or YouTube playback glitches
user_pains.evidence: Ads keep appearing on YouTube; the page must be refreshed before a video will play.

user_pains.pain: Hidden cookie banners make some sites unusable
user_pains.evidence: Sites won't respond until consent is given, but the banner is hidden, including in private browsing.

user_pains.pain: No way to configure what gets blocked
user_pains.evidence: Users ask for an option to choose what to block, especially to re-enable cookie pop-ups.
Worked for the first couple of days and then seemed no better; v1 stopped working on YouTube.
One reviewer says cookie windows always appear despite the blocker.
